Comments: No credible, specific evidence of a government-to-person (G2P) digital payment program at scale (e.g., social transfers disbursed to wallets/accounts with quantified coverage) was located in the prior targeted searches documented in workspace notes; therefore scored Unknown/NA per instruction.

revision_notes: Row was flagged Unknown with no source, but a single check surfaced an authoritative, dated World Bank brief confirming active, at-scale G2P digital disbursement, so the row was moved to the full verification path. The World Bank (brief dated 26 April 2024) reports that 44.4% of AMEN Social Programme cash transfers have been digitalised, with a Ministry of Social Affairs-Tunisian Post convention providing beneficiaries digital payment cards linked to e-wallets, and that the ~900,000-household COVID-19 emergency cash transfer round (2021) was delivered through a fully digital registration and disbursement process. This supports 'Yes - Active Use' (code 3) rather than Unknown; recalculated value code changed from 0 to 3.
revised_comments: Tunisia's government actively disburses social assistance digitally through the AMEN Social Programme, the country's flagship social protection scheme. As of 2024, 44.4% of AMEN cash transfers have been digitalised, delivered via digital payment cards linked to e-wallets provided through a partnership between the Ministry of Social Affairs and Tunisian Post. During the COVID-19 pandemic, emergency cash transfers reached roughly 900,000 low-income households through a fully digital registration and disbursement process. Further World Bank financing agreed in 2026 supports an Integrated Beneficiary Registry and the broadening of digital payment tools across social protection programmes, indicating an active but still-expanding digitisation of government-to-person payments rather than universal coverage.

revision_notes: Row was flagged Unknown with no source, but a single check surfaced the Central Bank of Tunisia's binding regulatory circular on payment system governance, so the row was moved to the full verification path. BCT Circular n°2024-5 (13 February 2024, read in full) mandates an audit and risk committee, an internal audit function, and an annual information-systems security audit for payment/securities-settlement system managers, with audit reports (Articles 26, 36, 73) submitted to the Central Bank rather than published; an earlier, still-relevant circular n°2018-16 (Article 10) imposes an equivalent annual IT security audit requirement, reported to BCT, on licensed payment establishments. Article 38 of the 2024 circular requires only a separate public annual activity report on governance/ownership/participation, not the audit results themselves. This supports 'Private Audits' (code 2), not Unknown; recalculated value code changed from 0 to 2.
revised_comments: Tunisia's Central Bank imposes mandatory independent audit requirements on payment system operators. Central Bank of Tunisia Circular n°2024-5 (13 February 2024), governing managers of payment systems and securities settlement-delivery systems, requires each system manager to establish a board-level audit and risk committee and an internal audit function, and to conduct an annual information-systems security audit whose reports are communicated to the Central Bank of Tunisia. An equivalent requirement for licensed payment establishments has applied since Circular n°2018-16 (Article 10), which likewise requires an annual IT security audit reported to the Central Bank. Operators must additionally publish a separate annual activity report covering ownership, governance and participation, but the detailed audit reports themselves remain confidential to the regulator rather than being made public.
